tagline: Germany's great port city — HADAG's harbour ferries are part of the HVV public-transport network on the Elbe.
summary: Hamburg is Germany's largest port and second-largest city, built along the tidal Elbe. The HADAG harbour ferries — lines 61 to 75, run by the city inside the HVV network — carry around nine million passengers a year from the Landungsbrücken piers across the working harbour to Finkenwerder, Blankenese, Teufelsbrück and the HafenCity waterfront. The city targets climate neutrality by 2045 and is testing hybrid and electric ferries. Every harbour leg is sheltered and well inside Pioneer II range, making Hamburg a strong public-transport waterway market with a clear decarbonization mandate.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the entire Hamburg harbour ferry network — every line from Landungsbrücken to Blankenese and Finkenwerder is sheltered and well inside the 70nm range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) could extend down the Elbe toward Stade or Cuxhaven beyond the harbour network.

competitive_landscape: HADAG runs the harbour ferries inside the HVV network. Navier is a passenger-only foiling layer above the existing service, complementing HADAG's move to hybrid and electric vessels.
regulatory_note: Strict low-wake operation in the residential western Elbe and careful coordination with heavy container-port traffic in the fairway; foiling only where the channel and wake rules allow.
